title: Probabilistic Stability Transfer for One-Dimensional Euler Characteristic Transforms
summary: The Euler characteristic transform (ECT) is a computable topological signature for shapes embedded in Euclidean space. Existing ECT stability results control changes in the transform through deterministic geometric perturbation bounds, but many data-generating mechanisms produce perturbations that are random and unbounded in the worst case. In such settings a uniform deterministic bound may be unavailable or too pessimistic. This paper formulates a probabilistic stability-transfer principle for one-dimensional ECT stability: a deterministic stability estimate is combined with a tail bound for the induced geometric error to obtain a high-probability ECT error bound. We instantiate this principle using the stability theorem of Marsh and Beers for embeddings of finite one-dimensional CW complexes. The resulting consequences cover ambient displacement fields conditionally on admissibility and supremum-tail estimates, and finite landmark perturbations with reconstruction. For landmark perturbations, bounded, sub-Gaussian, sub-exponential, and polynomial-tail noise assumptions give explicit high-probability ECT stability bounds. The framework isolates a geometric stochastic component that arises in shape analysis pipelines across biological morphology, medical imaging, molecular structure analysis, and remote sensing.

title: Disc-presheaves and normal invariants
summary: In this note, we elaborate on a result of Krannich--Kupers--Mehzer on Disc-presheaves. We show that equivalences of $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves of manifolds yields homotopy equivalences with trivial normal invariant. As an application, we show that two closed, simply connected manifolds are homeomorphic if and only if their $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves are equivalent.

title: On the Motivic K-Theories of Classifying Spaces of Cyclic 2-Groups
summary: We compute the $2$-completed integral motivic homology, effective algebraic $K$-theory, and very effective Hermitian $K$-theory of the geometric classifying spaces $Bμ_{2^n}$, $n\geq 2$, over algebraically closed and real closed fields. We first carry out the corresponding classical calculations and, then obtain the motivic results using motivic spectral sequences and comparison techniques. The results reveal the classical $2$-torsion together with motivic $τ$-periodicity and $ρ$-torsion.

title: Inscribed 4-polytopes of maximal volume with seven and eight vertices
summary: We prove, with sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, that every cyclic $4$-polytope with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $2/5$. Hence no $4$-polytope of maximal volume with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ is cyclic, answering a question of Horváth and Lángi for $d = 4$, and with their theorem the maximal volume is $\sqrt{3}/4$. With eight vertices, the same method bounds the volume of every simplicial type other than the cross-polytope by $13/20$, so the regular cross-polytope, of volume $2/3$, is up to orthogonal transformations the unique maximiser.

title: Complex Projective Spaces in Rational $SO(2)$-Equivariant Stable Homotopy Theory
summary:
We show that for almost every finite dimensional complex representation $W$ of $SO(2)$ the associated complex projective space $\mathbb{C}P(W)_+$ does not have the rational stable homotopy type of a specific wedge of representation spheres constructed from a chosen filtration of $\mathbb{C}P(W)_+$. This contrasts with the case for representations of finite Abelian groups where such an equivalence does hold.
  In the finite group case, the splitting result provides us with a classification result for projective spaces up to rational stable equivalence. In light of the non-splitting as a particular wedge of spheres in the case of projective spaces of $SO(2)$-representations, we also prove a separate classification theorem.

title: The Volume Exchange Metric
summary: The volume exchange metric between cell structures embedded in Euclidean space is introduced. Intuitively, it measures the minimum amount of volume that must be swept out to continuously transform one cell structure into another. The main result is that the volume exchange metric coincides with a discrete analogue defined as a minimum over matchings between cells. Algorithms are described to compute the discrete volume exchange metric and illustrate its effectiveness at distinguishing polycrystalline microstructures in computational experiments.

title: Orthogonal group sections via light bulb systems
summary: For any oriented, smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times S^2)^{\# n}\# D^4$, this paper shows that the natural group homomorphism $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\to \mathrm{O}(H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}))$$ admits a section. In fact, every light bulb system in $X$ gives rise to a section, which can be characterized uniquely in terms of implanted barbell twists and implanted crossbell involutions. Moreover, all sections arising from different light bulb systems become identical after a single $S^2\times S^2$--stabilization of $X$.

title: Homotopy Groups of Special Orthogonal Groups in Degrees 23 to 29
summary: This book presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n$, as well as some $π_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n))$, with explicit generators.

title: Littlewood's mutually touching cylinders: the maximum is seven
summary: We give a computer-assisted proof that eight congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ cannot touch pairwise. Since seven such cylinders exist, the maximum number of congruent mutually touching infinite cylinders is seven. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968.

title: Weak reducibility for bridge trisections
summary: A bridge splitting of a knot is weakly reducible if it has a pair of disjoint shadows, one from above and one from below, in the splitting surface. The process of weak reduction exchanges local minima and maxima in the splitting, untelescoping the splitting and giving a method for detecting essential surfaces in the knot complement. Bridge trisections generalize bridge splittings to the setting of surfaces in 4-manifolds. We define weak reducibility in this context, giving diagrammatic conditions for carrying out a weak reduction operation on bridge splittings. We produce a partial classification of 4-bridge trisections of surfaces in $S^4$.

title: Braid spaces have no geodesic loops
summary: The braid spaces are defined as universal metric coverings of the standard complex spaces, branched over certain hyperplane arrangements. We describe a natural family of convex functions on braid spaces and use them to prove that braid spaces contain no geodesic loops. This statement is a consequence of the well-known conjecture that every braid space is CAT(0).

title: U torsion structure in Heegaard Floer homology
summary: We construct infinite families of Brieskorn spheres with three singular fibers for which the difference between the largest and the second largest length of U-torsion in their Heegaard Floer homology $HF^-$ increases to infinity as the family parameter increases. In particular, these families give a negative answer to the strong geography restriction on rational homology spheres. As an application, these families give the examples of integer homology spheres that are neither surgery on a knot nor large surgery on links.

title: An orthogonality inequality in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$ and the double-cap conjecture
summary: The orthogonal neighborhood of a set in real projective space is the union of the hyperplanes perpendicular to its points. We prove that caps minimize neighborhood measure among measurable sets of fixed measure in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$, for $n \geq 3$, with rigidity up to null sets. This yields the double-cap conjecture: a measurable subset of $S^{n-1}$ containing no orthogonal pair has measure at most that of two opposite open caps of radius $π/4$. The argument combines compactness of the Funk transform, rotation comparisons, and projective variations. We also obtain qualitative stability and determine the measurable fractional chromatic number of the spherical orthogonality graph. AI played an assistive role in preparing this paper. The formalization and verification workflow for a separate Lean 4 proof of the main inequality and double-cap result, based on a different argument, were carried out almost entirely using AI-assisted tools.

title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
summary: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.

title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
summary: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.

title: Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families
summary: We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.

title: Median spaces with the strict separation property and superrigidity of actions
summary: We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.

title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
comment: 30 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Verification code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23504589
summary: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.
